title: QUIC RFC 9000 Preferred Address Field Shape Work Item
summary: Close the RFC 9000 S18P2 preferred_address field-shape proof gap with focused codec tests and a bounded preferred-address cutover proof.
planned_changes:
- Add focused requirement-home tests for preferred_address IPv4 and IPv6 address and port field sizes, network-byte-order preservation, both-family field presence, all-zero unused-family handling, stateless reset token association and length, and truncated-value rejection.
- Add focused requirement-home proof that the preferred_address transport parameter can effect the server-address change after preferred-address path validation succeeds and does not promote before validation.
- Add shared preferred_address requirement-home helpers for extracting and parsing the value shape.
- Add dedicated architecture and verification trace ownership for the selected S18P2 preferred_address requirements.
- Record existing transport-parameter benchmark coverage for preferred_address parse and format hot paths.
verification_plan: Run a Release build, run the focused S18P2 preferred_address requirement-home filter, run the adjacent preferred-address migration and transport-parameter fuzz regression filter, regenerate QUIC requirement coverage triage, validate SpecTrace JSON, run the full Release test suite without rebuilding, and check the resulting diff for whitespace errors.
out_of_scope: preferred_address connection-ID sequence and active_connection_id_limit accounting constraints already owned by ARC/WI/VER-QUIC-RFC9000-0031.
disable_active_migration preferred_address exception behavior already owned by ARC/WI/VER-QUIC-RFC9000-0062.
Full S9.6 preferred-address migration lifecycle beyond the bounded S18P2 server-address cutover pointer.
completion_notes: Completed as a focused transport-parameter field-shape and bounded cutover proof for the selected S18P2 preferred_address family.
